mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising real interest rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in INDPRO and a fall in HOUST over one month indicates supply chain inflation with reduced housing demand, which compresses corporate margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month AND HOUST < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in RSAFS above 1% for three months signals rising household savings and reduced consumption, which depresses corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases discount rates and reduces real equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in PAYEMS for two consecutive months signals weakening employment, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 65% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between GDPC1 growth and S&P 500 returns exists: when GDPC1 grows at > 2% q/q, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days are positive.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of quarters with GDPC1 > 2% q/q growth.
